message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to make live calls to external services or APIs, so I can’t pull up the current or future weather data for you. However, I can point you toward a few ways you could obtain that information yourself:

| Option | How to do it | What you’ll get |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| **OpenWeatherMap API** | Sign up for a free key at https://openweathermap.org/, then call the “One Call” endpoint with `lat=37.8651&lon=-119.5383&exclude=current,minutely,daily,alerts&units=imperial` (or `metric`). | Hourly forecasts for temperature, wind speed, precipitation probability, etc., for up to 48 h. For longer‑term forecasts you’d need the “5 day / 3 hour” endpoint or the paid “One Call 3‑hour” plan. |
| **NOAA Climate Data Online** | Use the NOAA API (https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/cdo-web/webservices/v2) with the station ID for the nearest weather station (e.g., GHCND:USW00023271). | Historical and near‑real‑time observations; the API also offers a “forecast” endpoint for short‑term predictions. |
| **Weather Underground** | If you have a Weather Underground account, use their API (https://api.weather.com/) with the latitude/longitude query. | Hourly and daily forecasts, plus radar imagery. |
| **Python libraries** | Install `requests` and call one of the above APIs directly from a script. Example: |

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "YOUR_OPENWEATHERMAP_KEY"
url = ("https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/onecall?"
       f"lat=37.8651&lon=-119.5383&exclude=current,minutely,daily,alerts"
       "&units=imperial&appid={API_KEY}")

resp = requests.get(url)
data = resp.json()
for hour in data["hourly"][:240]:   # 10 days × 24 hours
    print(hour["dt"], hour["temp"], hour["wind_speed"], hour.get("pop", 0))
```

If you’re looking for a quick visual look, you can also just open a browser and go to a site like https://www.accuweather.com/, enter “Yosemite National Park” or the coordinates, and view the 10‑day forecast there.
